newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-PACE TRIO THRUST AUSTRALIA TOWARDS VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PACE TRIO THRUST AUSTRALIA TOWARDS VICTORY.

text.p: Australia's fast bowlers, spearheaded by Glenn McGrath, thrust the touring team towards a second successive victory over England and a 2-1 lead in the Ashes series on Sunday.
McGrath struck twice and Paul Reiffel and Jason Gillespie took a wicket apiece as England, 329 behind on first innings, slipped to 102 for four at tea on the fourth day of the fourth test.
Australia declared their first innings on 501 for nine at lunch, left-handed opener Matthew Elliott having made an outstanding 199 to lead their recovery from 50 for four on the second day.
McGrath and Gillespie, coming down the slope at Headingley, found considerable lift and were also helped by other balls keeping low.

Mark Butcher, after making 19 from 18 balls in a positive start, edged McGrath to wicketkeeper Ian Healy, and in his next over a lifter accounted for Michael Atherton, caught by Shane Warne at third slip for two.
Alec Stewart (16) was confounded by the low bounce of a delivery from Reiffel that clipped the bottom of his bat and went into his stumps.
Even when Australia made two rare errors in the field, it cost them only a few runs.
Graham Thorpe, dropped by Steve Waugh, soon edged another chance to Healy, who could not grasp it but saw Mark Waugh react smartly to grab the rebound at second slip.
Thorpe had gone for 15, giving Gillespie a first wicket to follow his seven for 37 in the previous innings.
At tea, England's last two specialist batsmen were together, with Nasser Hussain on 38 and John Crawley on six.
Earlier, Australia batted on through the morning session, adding 128 in two hours for the loss of Elliott, Healy (31), Shane Warne (0) and Gillespie (3).

Even the last-wicket pair of Reiffel (54 not out) and McGrath (20 not out) added 40, both finishing just short of their highest scores in test cricket when skipper Mark Taylor declared at the interval.
